messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: Private VPC ingress/egress degraded for customer Horizon Enterprises (tenant=horizon-prod). Symptom: NLB health checks 502/timeout across two AZs. Notifying #eng-infra and #oncall. thread_ts=1768354321

maria.garcia: i'm on it. what changed in the vpc recently? :eyes: horizon-sre are you seeing app errors?

leo_ng: checking CloudTrail and security group deltas. found an automated run by infra-sync@ops at 2026-04-12T11:08:12Z that removed egress rule from sg-0f3d5a6b allowing 10.22.0.0/16 tcp 1024-65535. that would block ephemeral ports between NLB and targets.

sam_sec: removing ephemeral egress from a security group used by NLB targets will break health checks. please don't widen things to 0.0.0.0/0 unless necessary. get a rollback ready.

jess_cust: horizon-sre here: confirmed. at 11:09 UTC backend logs show connection resets and 502s for all traffic to private pool. impact: production traffic ~150 rps affected, some retries succeeding.

maria.garcia: mitigation suggestion: 1) immediate rollback of the SG egress delta 2) if rollback doesn't apply quickly, temporarily add egress specifically allowing NLB subnets/CIDR 3) notify customer of temporary network change. any other ideas?

leo_ng: i can rollback the SG rule within 90s. running command now:
```
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0f3d5a6b --protocol tcp --port 1024-65535 --cidr 10.22.0.0/16
```
incident-bot: ACTION: security-group-authorize requested by leo_ng at 2026-04-12T11:12:05Z

leo_ng: rollback applied. AWS shows egress rule restored. starting to see initial target health checks flip to healthy in AZ-a. monitoring: https://internal.monitoring/redwood/targets/horizon-prod

horizon-sre: health checks moved to healthy for AZ-a at 11:14 UTC, AZ-b recovering. user errors dropping. thanks.

jess_cust: customer reports partial recovery at 11:15. they want RCA and fix for automation.

maria.garcia: short summary: root cause appears to be infra-sync automation incorrectly pruning egress rules that are required by NLB-attached target SGs. immediate fix: reapply egress rule. followups: add safeguard in infra-sync to prevent removal of ephemeral egress from SGs tagged with "redwood:nlb-attachment"; add canary test to automation pipeline that simulates NLB health checks; schedule PM with Horizon.

sam_sec: opened security ticket SEC-2026-408 and flagged infra-sync owner. recommend code guard in repo to block changes that remove TCP 1024-65535 from NLB-related SGs.

leo_ng: filed PR to infra-sync repo to add guard: https://git.internal/infra-sync/pull/433. also adding a pre-deploy hook to run a quick connectivity check against a staging NLB.

maria.garcia: handoff note: next oncall please watch for target flapping for 60m. if more than 2 recurrences, escalate to eng-runtime + customer success. i'll attach timeline and commands to the ticket.

oncall-rtg: taking the watch window. thx. i've updated the rota and set an alert for 5x unhealthy events within 10m.

emily-ops: added post-incident tasks to backlog: infra-sync guard, canary test, customer comms, and PM meeting prep. owners assigned.

horizon-sre: quick question — would switching to ALB as failover help? we rely on sticky sessions there.

maria.garcia: ALB failover could work, but would need sticky session config and traffic shifting. not recommended as immediate workaround. long-term we can design multi-proxy failover with session affinity preserved.

jess_cust: scheduling postmortem 2026-04-13T15:00 UTC with infra, sec, eng-runtime, and Horizon SRE. i will draft impact statement and customer notes.

maria.garcia: closing thread here; incident mitigated. tagging incident-ticket: #incident-horizon-vpc-egress-20260412. will update ticket with full timeline and followups. ping me for regressions. :heart:

incident-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED at 2026-04-12T12:08:00Z by maria.garcia — root cause: automation removed ephemeral egress on NLB-attached SG; remediation: restored rules and hardened automation checks.
